summary: @ornikar/react-modern-calendar-datepicker 3.2.3 ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package presents itself as a fork of the react-modern-calendar-datepicker library, and lib/ plus README are the legitimate upstream sources. On top of that, package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, and setup.mjs (obfuscator.io-style renamed identifiers with per-function proxy string tables) detects the host platform, downloads a Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, chmod +x's it in a tmp directory, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. If a `bun` binary is already on PATH it is used directly. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with a custom string-array shuffle routine (`WV8StW`) and a >2000-entry constants table used to reconstruct identifiers and literals at runtime; its actual behavior cannot be recovered statically. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js are listed in the package.json `files` allowlist (`["lib","index.d.ts"]`) yet both are shipped in the tarball. Installing this version causes `npm install` to fetch a second language runtime and execute an opaque obfuscated payload on the installer's machine, unrelated to the advertised datepicker functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
